note: v3337: FOUR MORE CI REDS CLOSED, and only ONE was a code defect. ONE, and it is real: moduleFreshness ran inside status_payload untimed since v3288, so its cost landed in unattributedMs where nobody can act on it. It is now wrapped in _t like every neighbour. THE OTHER THREE WERE LAWS PINNING A SPELLING. test_heart_surface wanted the pre-hoist form of the owner lookup, which is the FOURTH law that one v3326 hoist broke. test_the_shelf_builds_what_it_shows wanted a one-line ghost guard that had gained a counter inside its braces, identical behaviour and different text. test_the_shelf_publishes located its subject with a regex demanding exact indentation, and v3289 both inserted a guard line and re-indented the block, so the law could not read its own subject and correctly FAILED rather than skipped. ⚠ THE OBVIOUS REPAIR FOR THAT LAST ONE WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED: a loosened try-to-catch regex matched an UNRELATED fetch block of 585,430 chars with unbalanced braces. It now anchors outward from the one unique line, asserts that line occurs exactly once, and checks the extracted block has balanced braces before believing a verdict taken from it. ⚠ AND A SECOND HARNESS FAULT WAS WEARING THE CLOTHES OF A FINDING: the runner printed nothing for the no-card case, because v3289 added an early return and node treats a top-level return in a CommonJS module as an exit, so the print after the block never ran. The block now runs inside an IIFE, where a return ends the block rather than the measurement. All four gates green, every changed law red-proved. ⚠ NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: the reels-before-charts law encodes his v2985 ruling that cards precede analytics, and v3289 knowingly moved highlights and the timeline above them with a measurement at 1120x660. That is two rulings in conflict, not a stale anchor, and rewriting a law to match a later change is not mine to do quietly.
